summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl 0; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Coffee +13.6%; weakest: KC wheat -15.3%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.12% (+11 bp in a month), 2-year 4.79% (+3 bp); 2s10s curve +33 bp (+8 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.06% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.80 (+1.4% in a month, +3.6% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.034 (-1.5% in a month): little changed. USD/CNY 6.664 (-0.5%); USD/MXN 18.66 (+8.4%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -0.2% in a month (+13.2% YTD); VIX 16.7. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 96.93 $/bbl (+8.7% in a month), Brent 108.56, ULSD 4.572 $/gal (+1.9%), natural gas 2.84 (-5.2%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -2.8% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.0%, Hang Seng -5.6%, yuan +0.5% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 14 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (42%); S&P GSCI +0.6% in a month; gold -5.3%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
